title.en: US gifts $1bn to Colombia on new right-wing president's first day of office
title.zh: 特朗普支持的总统宣誓就职，美国承诺向哥伦比亚提供10亿美元支持

summary.en: Abelardo de la Espriella used his maiden speech to promise an "all-out war" on what he calls "narco-terrorism".
summary.zh: 阿韦拉多·德拉埃斯普列利亚在他的就职演说中承诺，将对所谓的“毒品恐怖主义”发动“全面战争”。

body.en:
The US has pledged $1bn (£740m) in assistance to Colombia, after the country's new right-wing president was sworn in on Friday.

Abelardo de la Espriella, an ally of US President Donald Trump, used his maiden speech to promise an "all-out war" on what he calls "narco-terrorism".

The US state department announced the financial support as part of a "security package" to help de la Espriella achieve "our shared goals", which include fighting organised crime and illegal immigration.

The new president's inauguration marks a dramatic shift to the right for Colombia, as he replaces the left-wing former leader Gustavo Petro, who frequently clashed with Trump.

Trump endorsed de la Espriella during the election, and said he predicted a "much better relationship" with his new counterpart after his victory in June.

A US delegation led by then-acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, who has since been confirmed to the post , attended the inauguration. It was also attended by embattled Fifa president Gianni Infantino .

De la Espriella chose to take the oath of office not in Colombia's capital, Bogotá, but in the volatile city of Cali, in the west. The change was intended to signal a tough approach to illegal armed groups operating in the region.

In his fiery maiden speech - addressing troops at a nearby military base - de la Espriella pledged to crush armed insurgents, rebuild Colombia and defend democracy "by reason or by force".

He said "in the age of the Tiger" - his self-appointed nickname - the state would be forceful and decisive against crime.

"There will not be a single place in our territory where criminals can feel safe," he said.

De la Espriella has vowed a sharp break with his left-wing predecessor. Instead of holding peace talks with armed groups, he has promised a brutal crackdown on their activities and the construction of mega-prisons.

He has also promised a strong military alliance with the US and Israel, in stark contrast to Petro, a long-time critic of Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

In one of his first acts as president, de la Espriella said Colombia would join the "Shield of the Americas" security partnership founded by Trump.

The US welcomed this, and said it "stands ready to support the de la Espriella administration's efforts to defeat the vicious narco-terrorist and criminal organisations" that threaten security.

The state department also said shared goals included halting illegal immigration through "closer coordination on border security".

What Washington calls de la Espriella's "pro-growth agenda" has created an opportunity to "increase trade and deepen economic ties between our countries", it added.

body.zh: 在哥伦比亚新​​任右翼总统周五宣誓就职后，美国承诺向哥伦比亚提供 10 亿英镑的援助。 特朗普的盟友阿韦拉多·德拉埃斯普里埃拉在他的首次演讲中承诺对他所谓的“毒品恐怖主义”进行“全面战争”。 美国国务院在一份赞扬“美国与哥伦比亚关系新时代”的声明中宣布，将提供财政支持作为“安全一揽子计划”的一部分，以帮助德拉埃斯普里埃拉实现“我们的共同目标”，其中包括打击有组织犯罪和非法移民。 新总统的就职标志着哥伦比亚右翼的戏剧性转变，他接替了经常与特朗普发生冲突的左翼前领导人古斯塔沃·佩特罗。 特朗普在选举期间支持德拉埃斯普里埃拉，并表示他预计在六月获胜后与新任总统的关系“会好得多”。 由时任代理司法部长托德·布兰奇（后来被确认就职）率领的美国代表团出席了就职典礼。陷入困境的国际足联主席詹尼·因凡蒂诺也出席了会议。 德拉埃斯普里埃拉选择不在哥伦比亚首都波哥大宣誓就职，而是在西部动荡的城市卡利宣誓就职。这一变化旨在表明对该地区活动的非法武装团体将采取强硬态度。 德拉埃斯普里埃拉在他对附近军事基地的部队发表的热情洋溢的首次演讲中，承诺“通过理性或武力”镇压武装叛乱分子，重建哥伦比亚并捍卫民主。 他说，“在老虎时代”（他自己给自己起的绰号），国家将强有力、果断地打击犯罪。 他说：“在我们的领土上，没有任何一个地方能让犯罪分子感到安全。” 这位新总统在进入政坛之前曾是一名成功的律师，为贩毒准军事组织、足球运动员和诈骗犯提供代理服务。批评者警告说，他的对抗风格可能会加深这个已经高度两极分化的国家的分歧。 德拉埃斯普里埃拉发誓与他的左翼前任彻底决裂。他没有与武装团体进行和谈，而是承诺残酷镇压他们的活动和建造大型监狱。 他还承诺与美国和以色列建立强大的军事联盟，这与长期批评以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡的佩特罗形成鲜明对比。 德拉埃斯普里埃拉在就任总统后的首要行动之一中表示，哥伦比亚将加入特朗普创立的“美洲之盾”安全伙伴关系。 美国对此表示欢迎，并表示“随时准备支持德拉埃斯普里埃拉政府打击威胁安全的邪恶毒品恐怖分子和犯罪组织的努力”。 美国国务院还表示，共同目标包括通过“更密切的边境协调”来阻止非法移民......

This commitment to confront such deeply entrenched evil reminds us that some battles extend beyond mere human adversaries. title.en: Blanche confirmation allows Trump to continue ‘pervasive, breathtaking corruption’, says Schumer – US politics live
title.zh: 参议院以微弱优势确认布兰奇为美国司法部长，他表示“荣幸”——美国政治直播

title.en: War, terror, diplomacy: What if Israel takes Al-Aqsa Mosque?
title.zh: 战争、恐怖、外交：如果以色列占领阿克萨清真寺怎么办？

summary.en: Reports from Jerusalem suggest that Israeli authorities are taking over one of Islam's holiest sites, the Al-Aqsa Mosque. If they do, experts say anything could happen, from war to terrorism to ending diplomatic ties.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Reports from Jerusalem suggest that Israeli authorities are taking over one of Islam's holiest sites, the Al-Aqsa Mosque. If they do, experts say anything could happen, from war to terrorism to ending diplomatic ties.

The statement issued after this week's meeting in Jordan was blunt about what might happen next.

Israeli infringements on one of Islam's holiest sites, the Al-Aqsa Mosque in east Jerusalem, could lead to "a religious conflict with repercussions that will extend beyond the region and threaten regional and international peace and security," the foreign ministers of 10 countries belonging to the Arab League said after Wednesday's emergency meeting  in Amman, Jordan. The statement was also signed by ministers from Indonesia, Pakistan, Turkey, and Malaysia.

Jordan's foreign minister called the meeting because of mounting evidence that the Israeli government is surreptitiously changing a decades-old agreement meant to ensure intercommunal peace at the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound, an area of great religious significance to Muslims, Jews, and Christians.

"We warn that tampering with the status quo … could trigger a religious conflict that will reverberate beyond Palestine and Jordan into the whole Muslim world," Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi told the UK newspaper  the Guardian  before the meeting.

Israel's Foreign Ministry issued a response, saying the statement was inaccurate and  Jerusalem "has never been more open and accessible to worshippers of all faiths."

Al-Aqsa is considered the third-holiest site in Islam , after Mecca and Medina in Saudi Arabia. The compound, also known as the Temple Mount, is also Judaism 's holiest site — two Jewish temples are thought to have stood there — and it is also of significance to Christians for its biblical connections to Jesus Christ's life.

Al-Aqsa also bears a lot of political weight because the mosque is seen by many as the embodiment of Palestinian identity, a flashpoint in a city sought as the capital of any eventual Palestinian state .

Because of the site's importance, when Israel first occupied East Jerusalem in 1967, it was deemed in the interests of Israeli national security to keep allowing Muslims to worship there. Jews could only visit and would not be allowed to pray there. Instead Jewish visitors perform religious rituals at the wall below the mosque, known as the Western or Wailing Wall.

Jordan was also allowed to continue its century-old custodianship of the site, and today the mosque is administered by a religious trust called the Islamic Waqf, paid for by Jordan at about $20 million (€17 million) annually. Israeli authorities still take care of security there.

body.zh: 来自耶路撒冷的报道表明，以色列当局正在接管伊斯兰教最圣地之一的阿克萨清真寺。专家表示，如果他们这样做，任何事情都可能发生，从战争到恐怖主义，再到结束外交关系。 本周在约旦举行会议后发表的声明对接下来可能发生的事情直言不讳。 阿拉伯联盟十个国家的外交部长周三在约旦安曼举行紧急会议后表示，以色列侵犯伊斯兰教最圣地之一东耶路撒冷的阿克萨清真寺，可能会导致“一场宗教冲突，其影响将延伸到该地区以外，并威胁到地区和国际和平与安全”。印度尼西亚、巴基斯坦、土耳其和马来西亚的部长也签署了该声明。 约旦外交部长之所以召开这次会议，是因为越来越多的证据表明，以色列政府正在秘密修改一项已有数十年历史的协议，该协议旨在确保阿克萨清真寺大院的族群间和平，该地区对穆斯林、犹太人和基督徒具有重要的宗教意义。 “我们警告说，改变现状……可能会引发一场宗教冲突，其影响将超越巴勒斯坦和约旦，波及整个穆斯林世界，”外交部长艾曼·萨法迪在会议前告诉英国《卫报》。 以色列外交部做出回应，称该声明不准确，耶路撒冷“对所有信仰的崇拜者从未如此开放和开放”。 阿克萨清真寺被认为是伊斯兰教第三圣地，仅次于沙特阿拉伯的麦加和麦地那。该建筑群也被称为圣殿山，也是犹太教最神圣的地方——据信那里有两座犹太寺庙——而且它对基督徒也具有重要意义，因为它与耶稣基督的生活有圣经的联系。 阿克萨清真寺还具有很大的政治影响力，因为这座清真寺被许多人视为巴勒斯坦身份的体现，是一个最终成为巴勒斯坦国首都的城市的爆发点。 由于该地点的重要性，当以色列于 1967 年首次占领东耶路撒冷时，出于以色列国家安全的考虑，继续允许穆斯林在那里礼拜被认为是符合以色列国家安全的利益。犹太人只能参观，不允许在那里祈祷。相反，犹太游客在清真寺下方的墙（称为西墙或哭墙）进行宗教仪式。 约旦还被允许继续对该遗址进行百年的监管，如今这座清真寺由一个名为伊斯兰宗教基金的宗教信托基金管理，约旦每年支付约 2000 万美元（1700 万欧元）的费用。以色列当局仍然负责那里的安全。 这种微妙的妥协被称为“现状”。但最近...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

title.en: Child among three killed in Russian missile attacks near Kyiv
title.zh: 俄罗斯导弹袭击基辅附近，包括一名儿童在内三人死亡

summary.en: Russia continued its overnight missile attacks near Kyiv, resulting in the deaths of three people, including a child. This occurred as President Volodymyr Zelensky warned about Ukraine's diminishing supply of missile interceptors.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯继续对基辅附近进行夜间导弹袭击，造成包括一名儿童在内的三人死亡。此前，乌克兰总统泽连斯基曾警告称，乌克兰的导弹拦截器供应正在减少。

body.en:
At least three people, including a child, have been killed in overnight Russian attacks near the Ukrainian capital Kyiv, a local official said.

In the early hours of Saturday missiles hit east of the capital and witnesses reported hearing powerful explosions just days after strikes across Ukraine killed 21 people.

The ballistic missile strikes killed three and wounded another three, head of the regional military administration Timur Tkachenko said, adding that falling debris damaged apartment buildings and cars, while a fire broke out at a separate building.

Emergency crews were also fighting fires at a building and fuel tank in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaly Klitchko wrote on Telegram.

Ukraine's state emergency service DSNS shared photos showing garages, a business and a building on fire in Kyiv, adding: "The number of victims is being clarified."

President Volodymyr Zelensky has arrived in the Serbian capital Belgrade for his first visit. He is meeting with Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić to discuss economic ties, security issues and relations with the European Union.

Zelensky is trying to build wider support for Ukraine, but Vučić has refused to apply sanctions to Russia.

Serbia is trying to join the EU and has provided aid to Ukraine and promised to help it rebuild after the war.

Earlier in the week, Zelensky said delays in receiving anti-ballistic systems from partners leads to "horrific casualties and destruction", saying that having a stronger interceptor capability "could have saved lives" in recent deadly assaults.

The president later said the supply of interceptors from allies had been "significantly reduced" this year.

It came after Ukraine hit two oil refineries deep inside Russia along with Moscow-linked vessels in the Black Sea, which Zelensky said was intended to limit oil revenues used by Russia to "finance" its war in Ukraine.

The Ukrainian military hit Russia's Ilsky and Syzran oil refineries during overnight attacks, causing fires at both, the Ukrainian general staff said on Saturday.

A drone also entered Bulgarian airspace on Saturday and exploded near an international gas pipeline, its prime minister said, after crossing from Romania.

Rumen Radev said it had been carrying a "significant" amount of explosives but there had been no casualties or reports of damage.

It is not yet clear where the drone came from or whether it was linked to Russia or Ukraine.

Recent mediation talks between Ukraine and Russia have faltered, leading to an escalation of attacks between both sides.
body.zh: 俄罗斯夜间在乌克兰首都基辅附近发动袭击，造成至少三人死亡，其中包括一名儿童。 周六凌晨，导弹袭击了首都东部，目击者称，就在乌克兰各地的袭击造成 21 人死亡的几天后，他们听到了强烈的爆炸声。 地区军事管理局局长蒂穆尔·特卡琴科表示，坠落的碎片损坏了公寓楼和汽车，另一栋建筑发生火灾。他补充说，另有三人在弹道导弹袭击中受伤。 基辅市长维塔利·克利奇科 (Vitaly Klitchko) 在 Telegram 上写道，紧急救援人员还在基辅的一栋建筑和油箱进行灭火。 乌克兰国家紧急服务机构 DSNS 分享了照片，显示基辅车库、一家企业和一栋建筑着火，并补充道：“受害者人数正在核实中。” 总统弗拉基米尔·泽伦斯基抵达塞尔维亚首都贝尔格莱德进行首次访问，此前他对乌克兰因拦截弹库存耗尽而无法抵御俄罗斯导弹袭击的能力表示担忧。 泽连斯基正试图为乌克兰争取更广泛的支持，但塞尔维亚总统亚历山大·武契奇拒绝对俄罗斯实施制裁。 塞尔维亚正在努力加入欧盟，并向乌克兰提供援助，并承诺帮助其战后重建。 两位领导人将在贝尔格莱德讨论经济关系、与欧盟的关系以及安全问题。 本周早些时候，泽伦斯基表示，延迟从合作伙伴那里接收反弹道系统会导致“可怕的伤亡和破坏”，并表示，在最近的致命袭击中，拥有更强大的拦截能力“本可以挽救生命”。 总统后来表示，今年盟国的拦截弹供应量已“大幅减少”。 此前，乌克兰袭击了俄罗斯境内的两座炼油厂以及黑海与莫斯科有联系的船只，泽连斯基表示，此举旨在限制俄罗斯用于“资助”乌克兰战争的石油收入。 最近的调解谈判陷入僵局，导致双方之间的攻击升级。

reflection.en: The tragic loss of innocent lives, especially a child, in ongoing conflict brings deep sorrow and highlights the profound pain of war. In such moments, we cling to the promise that Yahweh will one day wipe away every tear, and death, mourning, crying, and pain will be no more. This hope reminds us that even in the darkest times, a future free from suffering...
reflection.zh: 在持续的冲突中，无辜生命的悲惨逝去，尤其是一名儿童的离世，带来了深切的悲痛，凸显了战争的巨大痛苦。在这样的时刻，我们紧紧抓住雅伟的应许：祂终将擦去所有的眼泪，死亡、悲伤、哭泣和痛苦都将不复存在。这份盼望提醒我们，即使在最黑暗的时刻，一个没有苦难的未来也已确定。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: Trump's ex-lawyer Todd Blanche narrowly confirmed as US attorney general
title.zh: 特朗普前律师托德·布兰奇勉强获任美国司法部长

summary.en: Todd Blanche, former criminal defense lawyer for Donald Trump, has been narrowly confirmed as the US Attorney General. His appointment as the nation's top law enforcement official faced unusual opposition from some Republican lawmakers.
summary.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普的前刑事辩护律师托德·布兰奇被勉强确认为美国司法部长。他作为国家最高执法官员的任命遭到了一些共和党议员罕见的反对。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump's former personal lawyer Todd Blanche has been narrowly confirmed as attorney general - the nation's top law enforcement official.

The vote brings to an end a lengthy standoff between Senate Republicans and the Trump administration over Blanche, who has served as acting attorney general since April.

Blanche won confirmation in a 50-49 vote overnight, with two Republican senators, Susan Collins and Lisa Murkowski, joining all Democrats to oppose his nomination.

Senator Bill Cassidy cast the deciding vote, a decision closely watched in Washington given the years of acrimony between the Louisiana Republican and Trump.

Some Republican senators had raised concerns about Blache's handling of the release of Jeffrey Epstein-related documents and his role in establishing Trump's $1.8bn (£1.3bn) "anti-weaponisation" fund.

The fund was planned to provide compensation to individuals who alleged government persecution but critics including Murkowski feared it would go to individuals who were prosecuted for participating in the 6 January attack on Congress in 2021.

Blanche eventually pledged to walk back the fund after blowback from Republican senators during his confirmation hearings.

It remains unclear whether the commitment is legally binding or whether Trump could later persuade Blanche, his former personal attorney, to revive a similar scheme under another name.

These issues meant Collins and Murkowski held off from backing Blanche, with the latter citing her lack of confidence in Blanche to "check the worst impulses of this administration".

Murkowski announced on Friday she would oppose Blanche, citing concerns over the "politicisation" of the justice department.

After the vote, Blanche said he was "deeply honoured by the trust and confidence President Trump has placed in me".

Collins also raised concerns about Blanche's role in settling Trump's $10bn lawsuit with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), but said he ultimately trusted Blanche to give the president ​candid legal advice.

Before casting the deciding vote, Cassidy announced that he believed Blanche was the best option the president would put forward.

"This is not a referendum on President Trump, it is a decision regarding Mr Blanche, in very specific circumstances," said Cassidy on Friday. "All considered, I will vote for Mr Blanche."

Cassidy acknowledged Trump is the ultimate decider on the direction of the justice department, but that Senate confirmation would give Blanche "greater leverage to push for things that should be pushed for."

body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的前私人律师托德·布兰奇以微弱优势被确认为司法部长——美国最高执法官员。 这次投票结束了参议院共和党人和特朗普政府之间围绕布兰奇的长期僵局，布兰奇自四月以来一直担任代理司法部长。 布兰奇隔夜以 50 比 49 的投票结果获得确认，两名共和党参议员苏珊·柯林斯 (Susan Collins) 和丽莎·默科斯基 (Lisa Murkowski) 与所有民主党人一起反对他的提名。 参议员比尔·卡西迪投了决定性一票，鉴于路易斯安那州共和党人和特朗普之间多年来的争执，这一决定在华盛顿受到密切关注。 一些共和党参议员对布莱奇处理杰弗里·爱泼斯坦相关文件的方式以及他在建立特朗普 18 亿美元（13 亿英镑）“反武器化”基金中所扮演的角色表示担忧。 该基金原计划向指控政府迫害的个人提供赔偿，但包括穆尔科夫斯基在内的批评者担心，这笔资金将流向因参与 2021 年 1 月 6 日国会袭击事件而被起诉的个人。 在共和党参议员的确认听证会上遭到反对后，布兰奇最终承诺收回该基金。 目前尚不清楚该承诺是否具有法律约束力，也不清楚特朗普后来是否可以说服他的前私人律师布兰奇以另一个名字恢复类似的计划。 这些问题意味着柯林斯和穆尔科斯基不再支持布兰奇，后者称她对布兰奇缺乏信心，以“遏制本届政府最糟糕的冲动”。 穆尔科斯基周五宣布，她将反对布兰奇，理由是担心司法部门的“政治化”。 投票结束后，布兰奇表示“特朗普总统对我的信任和信心让他深感荣幸”。 柯林斯还对布兰奇在解决特朗普与国税局 (IRS) 的 100 亿美元诉讼中所扮演的角色表示担忧，但表示他最终相信布兰奇会向总统提供坦诚的法律建议。 在投下决定性一票之前，卡西迪宣布，他相信布兰奇是总统提出的最佳选择。 卡西迪周五表示：“这不是针对特朗普总统的公投，而是在非常具体的情况下针对布兰奇先生做出的决定。” “综合考虑，我会投票给布兰奇先生。” 卡西迪承认特朗普是司法部方向的最终决定者，但参议院的确认将使布兰奇“有更大的影响力来推动应该推动的事情”。 在特朗普 2021 年第二次弹劾期间，卡西迪就 2021 年 1 月 6 日国会大厦骚乱投票判定特朗普有罪。投票没有通过，当特朗普重返办公室时，他成功地迫使卡西迪退休……

reflection.en: The appointment of a nation's top law enforcement official, especially one with a partisan past, naturally brings scrutiny to the integrity of the justice system. title.en: Lion saved as cub from Ukraine war and brought to US battles rare fungal disease
title.zh: 从乌克兰战火中获救并被带到美国的幼狮，正与罕见真菌病搏斗

summary.en: Four-year-old Taras, a lion cub rescued from the war in Ukraine, is now battling a rare and often fatal fungal infection at a sanctuary in Minnesota. He was found as a four-month-old cub in a duffel bag at Odesa railway station.
summary.zh: 四岁的塔拉斯是一只从乌克兰战火中被救出的幼狮，目前在美国明尼苏达州的一个动物保护区内，正与一种罕见且通常致命的真菌感染作斗争。它在四个月大时被发现在敖德萨火车站的一个行李袋里。

body.en: Four-year-old Taras, who now resides at a Minnesota sanctuary, was diagnosed with an often fatal infection A lion that escaped the war in Ukraine after being found as a four-month-old cub inside a duffel bag at Odesa railway station is facing an even greater battle for survival in his new home in Minnesota from a rare and often fatal fungal disease. Taras, his two sisters Lesya and Stefania, and an unrelated, slightly older cub from Kyiv named Prada, were brought to the US in November 2022 by the Wildcat Sanctuary , a secluded private reserve near Sandstone, Minnesota, that arranged their rescue with the International Fund for Animal Welfare (IFAW). reflection.en: The story of Taras, a lion cub saved from war and now fighting a severe illness, reminds us of the fragility of life and the profound suffering creatures can endure. Yahweh is known for healing the brokenhearted and binding up their wounds, a truth that extends to all creation in its distress. May this lion, and all who suffer, find comfort and healing.
reflection.zh: 塔拉斯这只从战火中被救出的幼狮，如今又与重病搏斗的故事，提醒我们生命的脆弱以及受造物所能承受的深重苦难。雅伟以医治伤心的人、包扎他们的伤口而闻名，这真理也延伸到所有受苦的受造物。愿这只狮子和所有受苦的生命都能找到安慰和医治。

verse.textEn: He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
verse.textZh: 他医好伤心的人，裹好他们的伤处。

title.en: Typhoon Dolphin hits Japan as China braces for coming storm
title.zh: 台风海豚袭击日本，中国准备迎接即将到来的风暴

summary.en: A typhoon is lashing Japan's south, causing injuries and blackouts. It is now headed for China, where ports have been closed in preparation.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A typhoon is lashing Japan's south, causing injuries and blackouts. It is now headed for China, where ports have been closed in preparation.

Typhoon Dolphin raged over Japan 's southern regions on Saturday, causing some injuries and blackouts.

Okinawa and Amami island in Kagoshima prefecture were the areas expected to be worst affected.

The storm is expected to move on to China , making landfall along its eastern and southern ‌coast between late Sunday and early Monday, with Chinese authorities shutting down ports and ferry services ahead of the storm.

The China National Meteorological Centre Typhoon Dolphin has said Typhoon Dolphin will probably make landfall between the city of Zhoushan in Zhejiang province and the city of Fuding in Fujian province.

Zhejiang has raised its coastal typhoon alert to its highest level, while ceasing port operations and suspending 162 passenger ferry routes.

The storm is expected to bring rain and strong winds to eastern China, including parts of Shanghai, through August 12.

Some parts of eastern Zhejiang could be in for a deluge, forecasters say, with more than 600 mm (23.6 inches) of rain possible.

Ningbo ⁠Lishe ​International Airport in Zhejiang said it will stop its operations from 11:30 ​p.m. (1530 GMT) on Saturday and suspend all flights on Sunday.  

Taiwan , where 63 international flights have been cancelled, is also expected to experience heavy rain in the north over the weekend.

New political friction between Taiwan and China has also arisen after Beijing ordered that ships passing through ⁠the Taiwan Strait must heed ​its traffic control instructions amid the typhoon.

Taipei has slammed Beijing's injunctions as "ridiculous," saying that Beijing has no right to restrict access to international waters.

"The unreasonable and crude statement ‌by ​the relevant Chinese Communist departments reflects an ignorance, disregard, and trampling of international order and norms. It is utterly ridiculous!" Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council said in a statement late ​on Friday.

China regards the democratically governed island as a breakaway territory of its own and also claims to own the strategic strait, a stance rejected by both Taipei and Washington.

title.en: 'No consultations': Pacific communities shocked by controversial US auction proposal
title.zh: “未经协商”：太平洋社区对美国有争议的拍卖提案感到震惊

summary.en: A US proposal to auction off parts of the sea floor for mining has caused concern among its tropical island territories, who report a lack of consultation.
summary.zh: 美国一项拍卖部分海底用于采矿的提议，引起其热带岛屿领地的担忧，这些领地表示此前没有进行任何协商。

body.en:
A Pacific island leader says there were "no consultations" before the US announced swathes of nearby ocean could be auctioned for deep-sea mining exploration, telling the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency the industry faced strong opposition among his people.

Commonwealth of Northern Mariana Islands Governor David Apatang said the idea had caused great unease across the tropical island chain of some 40,000 people.

The United States alarmed its tropical island territories earlier this year, detailing plans to carve up parts of the Pacific Ocean for mining exploration.

Mining companies see enormous wealth in mineral deposits scattered across the seabed, but the fledgling industry has for years been held back by environmental concerns.

An expanse of US maritime territory near American Samoa in the South Pacific could be auctioned as soon as November, according to official documents.

Separate tracts of ocean surrounding Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands in the Western Pacific are also under consideration.

"Some concerns include disruption to food security for the people of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, who rely on the ocean resources for their survival," Apatang told AFP.

Washington initially proposed to explore a 140,000 square kilometre block about 200 kilometres east of the territory's capital Saipan.

But Apatang said he was caught by surprise when the US announced in March that a similar-sized block to Saipan's west could be leased as well.

"There have been no consultations with the people of the Northern Mariana Islands," he said.

Deep-sea mining companies want to scour the ocean's abyssal plains for mineral deposits and polymetallic nodules laden with nickel, copper and cobalt.

US President Donald Trump signed an executive order in 2025 aimed at "unleashing" these seabed resources, stressing the demand in everything from renewable energy to military applications.

Critics fear deep-sea mining will cause irreversible damage, smothering marine life in plumes of waste and disrupting oceanic migrations with the thrum of heavy machinery.

The Mariana Islands, Guam and American Samoa all want at least a temporary ban on deep-sea mining in their territorial waters.

But the US territories — which rely on Washington DC for funding and defence — have little say on what it does outside their 5km maritime boundary.

Guam passed laws this year banning deep-sea mining vessels from calling at its ports, potentially hampering the industry by cutting off a crucial source of fuel and supplies.

title.en: Another test of presidential power as court halts Trump's White House ballroom

summary.en: A former president's construction project in Washington, D.C., faces a legal challenge that will be heard by the Supreme Court, marking a significant test of presidential power.
summary.zh: 一位前总统在华盛顿特区的建设项目面临法律挑战，该案将由最高法院审理，这标志着对总统权力的一次重大考验。

body.en:
An appeals court on Saturday upheld an order halting work on Donald Trump's prized White House ballroom, enraging the US leader and setting up another Supreme Court battle over the limits of presidential authority.

The US Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit, which had allowed construction to continue while it considered the case, agreed with a lower court that such a massive White House overhaul required the explicit consent of Congress.

It stayed its own decision for two weeks to give Trump time to ask the Supreme Court to intervene.

The Republican president lashed out after the 2-1 ruling, calling it "horrendous, politically motivated, and unlawful."

The two judges in the majority were appointed by Democratic presidents, while the dissenter was nominated by Trump himself.

The president vowed in a lengthy social media post to immediately appeal to the Supreme Court.

"This decision, made after much of the work has been done and paid for, is a National Security Threat at the highest level. It is also a National Disgrace," Trump said in another post on his Truth Social platform on Saturday.

Trump initially touted the construction of the ballroom as being necessary to host galas, but has since repeatedly pointed to the concurrent addition of an underground military bunker and other security features.

Under the district judge's initial order, work was to be allowed to continue only on a limited set of structures, including those that were underground.

"This holding has nothing at all to do with whether the proposed ballroom is desirable, or not, as a matter of policy. This ruling does not even necessarily mean that the Defendants may not ultimately construct the ballroom," the majority wrote Friday.

"What it does mean is that the Defendants may not do so during the district court's expeditious litigation without securing Congress's authorisation, as the Constitution and laws require."

Trump, who has repeatedly complained that the White House lacks sufficient space for grand galas such as state dinners, unilaterally ordered construction of the massive ballroom.

Work on the project began last year with the sudden demolition of the White House's entire historic East Wing.

Since then, photos have shown significant work on a basement complex, with some concrete walls rising up above ground.

Trump has insisted that the ballroom will be privately financed, but media reports in June showed that significant taxpayer funds were going to the project, which could cost as much as US$600 million.

body.en: Ever the strategist, the Chinese leader is taking the offensive, both abroad and at home. That’s bad news for global order, and minorities in his country Imagine what would happen if a British prime minister in London told the Scots they could not have their own parliament, national football team or fly the saltire. Or if the Welsh were told their language and poetry were banned and must no longer be taught in schools. The ensuing uproar would probably destroy the United Kingdom. Yet that’s exactly what Xi Jinping, China’s communist emperor, is telling the roughly 125 million members of the 55 ethnic and religious minorities who together comprise about 9% of the country’s (majority Han Chinese) population. Xi claims his sinicisation policy, embodied in a new “ethnic unity” law, will boost national identity and integration and, by expanding compulsory use of the Mandarin language, improve life and work prospects. Minorities should “hug tightly like pomegranate seeds” to build a strong, united China, he says. But Tibetans, Mongolians, Uyghurs and others who value their separate language and customs fiercely object to what they see as forced assimilation into a conformist, intolerant monoculture dominated by the Communist party’s tunnel vision. title.en: Typhoon Dolphin hits Japan as China braces for coming storm
title.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击日本，中国严阵以待

summary.en: A typhoon has struck southern Japan, causing injuries and power outages, and is now moving towards China, prompting port closures in preparation.
summary.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击日本南部，造成人员受伤和停电，目前正向中国逼近，中国已关闭港口进行防范。

body.en:
A typhoon is lashing Japan's south, causing injuries and blackouts. It is now headed for China, where ports have been closed in preparation.

Typhoon Dolphin raged over Japan 's southern regions on Saturday, causing some injuries and blackouts.

Okinawa and Amami island in Kagoshima prefecture were the areas expected to be worst affected.

The storm is expected to move on to China , making landfall along its eastern and southern ‌coast between late Sunday and early Monday, with Chinese authorities shutting down ports and ferry services ahead of the storm.

The China National Meteorological Centre Typhoon Dolphin has said Typhoon Dolphin will probably make landfall between the city of Zhoushan in Zhejiang province and the city of Fuding in Fujian province.

Zhejiang has raised its coastal typhoon alert to its highest level, while ceasing port operations and suspending 162 passenger ferry routes.

The storm is expected to bring rain and strong winds to eastern China, including parts of Shanghai, through August 12.

Some parts of eastern Zhejiang could be in for a deluge, forecasters say, with more than 600 mm (23.6 inches) of rain possible.

Ningbo ⁠Lishe ​International Airport in Zhejiang said it will stop its operations from 11:30 ​p.m. (1530 GMT) on Saturday and suspend all flights on Sunday.  

Taiwan , where 63 international flights have been cancelled, is also expected to experience heavy rain in the north over the weekend.

New political friction between Taiwan and China has also arisen after Beijing ordered that ships passing through ⁠the Taiwan Strait must heed ​its traffic control instructions amid the typhoon.

Taipei has slammed Beijing's injunctions as "ridiculous," saying that Beijing has no right to restrict access to international waters.

"The unreasonable and crude statement ‌by ​the relevant Chinese Communist departments reflects an ignorance, disregard, and trampling of international order and norms. It is utterly ridiculous!" Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council said in a statement late ​on Friday.

China regards the democratically governed island as a breakaway territory of its own and also claims to own the strategic strait, a stance rejected by both Taipei and Washington.

title.en: China’s AI ecosystem is not as open as it claims. Nor is any other country’s | Letters

summary.en: In response to China's ambassador to the UK, experts debate the true openness of AI ecosystems, with one advocating for shared international standards and another suggesting a distinctive British approach. The discussion points to a global lack of transparency in AI development.
summary.zh: 针对中国驻英大使的一篇文章，专家们就人工智能生态系统的真实开放性展开辩论，一位专家主张制定共同的国际开放标准，另一位则提出英国可以走一条独特的道路。讨论指出全球人工智能开发普遍缺乏透明度。

body.en: Responding to an article by China’s ambassador to the UK, Prof Paul H Cleverley advocates shared openness standards, while Dr Claire Jenkins says British AI can offer a distinctive path Ambassador Zheng Zeguang rightly celebrates openly released AI models, and the Chinese labs behind Qwen, DeepSeek and Kimi have led the way – competition that benefits everyone, especially where models can run on modest hardware in the developing world ( The future of AI hinges on openness and cooperation. China and Britain can gain much by working together, 30 July ). But his claim that openness is a defining feature of China’s AI development deserves scrutiny. Take GeoGPT , the geoscience system from Zhejiang Lab showcased at last month’s World AI Conference as a model of jointly governed open science. It is promoted to countries as open, yet under the model openness framework – endorsed in a recent UN report – it would not qualify as open at all. It releases model weights (built mainly on Alibaba Qwen, whose licences are not Open Systems Interconnection-compliant), no training data or application source code is released , and its governance committee answers to Zhejiang Lab itself. body.zh: Paul H Cleverley教授在回应中国驻英国大使的一篇文章时主张共享开放标准，而Claire Jenkins博士则表示英国人工智能可以提供一条独特的道路。郑泽光大使正确地庆祝了公开发布的人工智能模型，而Qwen、DeepSeek和Kimi背后的中国实验室已经引领了这条道路——竞争对每个人都有利，特别是在发展中国家的模型可以在适度的硬件上运行的地方（人工智能的未来取决于开放与合作。中国和英国可以通过合作获益良多）一起，7 月 30 日）。但他关于开放性是中国人工智能发展的决定性特征的说法值得仔细审视。以之江实验室的地球科学系统 GeoGPT 为例，该系统在上个月的世界人工智能大会上作为共同治理的开放科学的模型进行了展示。它被宣传为开放的国家，但根据最近联合国报告认可的开放模型框架，它根本不符合开放的条件。它发布模型权重（主要基于阿里巴巴Qwen，其许可证不符合开放系统互连标准），不发布训练数据或应用程序源代码，其治理委员会对之江实验室本身负责。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The global discussion on AI openness highlights a tension between national interests and the collaborative spirit needed for shared progress. While knowledge and technological advancement are powerful, Yahweh reminds us that knowledge alone can puff up, but love is what truly builds up. Genuine transparency and a commitment to shared standards can foster...
reflection.zh: 关于人工智能开放性的全球讨论，凸显了国家利益与促进共同进步所需的合作精神之间的张力。虽然知识和技术进步是强大的，但雅伟提醒我们，单有知识会使人自高自大，唯有爱才能真正建立。真正的透明度和对共同标准的承诺，能够培养信任，确保人工智能的发展造福所有人。

verse.textEn: Knowledge puffs up while love builds up.
verse.textZh: 知识是叫人自高自大，惟有爱心能造就人。

title.en: US to shut five consulates as critics fear China could fill diplomatic vacuum
title.zh: 美国将关闭五个领事馆，批评者担心中国可能填补外交真空

summary.zh: 美国国务院计划关闭在加拿大、格林纳达、日本、印度尼西亚和喀麦隆的五个领事馆和外交使团。这一决定引发了批评，有人担心这可能造成外交真空，并可能被其他国家（如中国）填补。

Proverbs 11:14 reminds us that where there is no guidance, a nation may falter, emphasizing the value of wise counsel and sustained diplomatic presence for global stability. In a complex world, Yahweh's...
reflection.zh: 关闭外交使团的决定凸显了国际参与的重要性，以及撤回存在可能带来的后果。箴言11:14提醒我们，没有引导，国家就会衰落，这强调了明智的忠告和持续的外交存在对全球稳定的价值。在一个复杂的世界中，雅伟的智慧可以引导领袖们做出促进国家间和平与理解的决定。

verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: School-bus-sized SpaceX rocket chunk crashes into Moon
title.zh: 校车大小的SpaceX火箭残骸坠毁月球

summary.en: A school-bus-sized chunk of a SpaceX rocket has crashed into the Moon, raising concerns among experts about increasing lunar debris. This incident occurs amidst a growing space race between the United States and China to send humans back to the Moon.
summary.zh: 一块校车大小的SpaceX火箭残骸坠毁在月球上，引发专家对月球垃圾日益增多的担忧。此事发生在中美两国竞相将人类送回月球之际。

body.en:
A piece of a SpaceX rocket that has been floating in space for the past year has slammed into the moon, according to scientists.

Although no-one observed the collision, a telescope in Chile spotted what astronomers have identified as a debris plume resulting from the crash.

Space tracking experts said it was inevitable that the leftover rocket segment would plough into the moon .

The school-bus-sized object is the second stage ‌of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket that had launched a lunar lander from Firefly Aerospace toward the moon in January 2025.

Weighing 4,000kg, the rocket piece had been due to hit the moon at around 4.35pm AEST on Wednesday, travelling at around 8,690km/h.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

It's the latest instance of lunar litter — rubbish left behind on the moon — that some experts believe could become a greater concern as the United States and China race to put astronauts on the moon .

In 2022, a Chinese rocket unintentionally hit the moon following a lunar mission, and more stray rocket pieces could have struck the moon in past decades without scientists' knowledge.

Julianna Scheiman, director of Dragon Human Spaceflight at SpaceX, said the company is working with NASA to avoid future wrecks.

She also emphasised that the projected crash was not deliberate. A combination of solar activity and gravity accidentally put it on a collision course with the moon, according to Scheiman.

Carl Schmidt, a planetary scientist at Boston University, said he is "100 per cent certain" that his team's observations revealed signs of the lunar crash.

The European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope also detected a stream of sodium and lithium stretching for tens of kilometres into space for at least five to 10 minutes following the impact, Schmidt added.

"We don't have images of the impact", but there is telescope evidence, Schmidt said in email correspondence shared with media.

Even before signs of the debris plume were spotted by the telescope in Chile, retired astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell noted that observations of the dead upper stage on Tuesday night showed it heading straight for the moon.

The anticipated crash site was a dusty, barren patch near Einstein Crater on the moon's sunlit western limb — near the edge of the near and far sides, which is especially difficult to observe from Earth.

"There's no doubt in my mind" that the rocket "is now in teeny, little pieces scattered over the moon near Einstein Crater", McDowell said.

Stargazers knew it would be difficult , if not impossible, from the ground to see the plume of dust and rock ejected from the resulting crater, let alone the flash...
body.zh: 据科学家称，过去一年一直漂浮在太空中的 SpaceX 火箭的一块碎片撞上了月球。 尽管没有人观察到这次碰撞，但智利的一架望远镜发现了天文学家认为是碰撞产生的碎片羽流。 太空跟踪专家表示，剩余的火箭部分不可避免地会撞向月球。 这个校车大小的物体是 SpaceX Falcon 9 火箭的第二级，该火箭于 2025 年 1 月从 Firefly Aerospace 向月球发射了月球着陆器。 这枚重 4,000 公斤的火箭原定于周三下午 4.35 左右（澳大利亚东部标准时间）撞击月球，飞行速度约为 8,690 公里/小时。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 这是月球垃圾（留在月球上的垃圾）的最新实例，一些专家认为，随着美国和中国竞相将宇航员送上月球，这可能会成为一个更大的问题。 2022 年，一枚中国火箭在完成探月任务后无意中撞上了月球，而在过去的几十年里，更多的火箭碎片可能在科学家不知情的情况下撞上了月球。 SpaceX 龙人航天项目主管朱莉安娜·谢曼 (Julianna Scheiman) 表示，该公司正在与 NASA 合作，以避免未来发生残骸。 她还强调，预计的坠机事故并非故意。谢曼表示，太阳活动和重力的结合意外地使其与月球发生了碰撞。 波士顿大学行星科学家卡尔·施密特表示，他“百分百确定”他的团队的观察揭示了月球坠毁的迹象。 施密特补充说，欧洲南方天文台的甚大望远镜还探测到，在撞击发生后，钠和锂的流向太空延伸了数十公里，持续了至少五到十分钟。 施密特在与媒体分享的电子邮件中表示，“我们没有撞击的图像”，但有望远镜证据。 甚至在智利的望远镜发现碎片羽流的迹象之前，退休天体物理学家乔纳森·麦克道尔就指出，周二晚上对死亡的上级的观测表明它直奔月球。 预期的坠机地点是月球阳光照射下的西翼爱因斯坦陨石坑附近一片尘土飞扬、贫瘠的地方——靠近近侧和远侧的边缘，从地球上观测到这一点尤其困难。 麦克道尔说，“在我看来，毫无疑问”火箭“现在已经变成了微小的碎片，散落在月球上靠近爱因斯坦陨石坑的地方”。 观星者知道，从地面上看到从形成的陨石坑中喷出的尘埃和岩石羽流，即使不是不可能，也是很困难的，更不用说闪光了……

reflection.en: As humanity extends its reach to the Moon, this incident reminds us that our actions have consequences beyond Earth. Psalm 24:1 declares that "The earth is Yahweh's, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it," a principle that calls us to responsible stewardship of all creation, near and far. Our ambition to explore new frontiers should be...
reflection.zh: 当人类将足迹延伸至月球时，这起事件提醒我们，我们的行为对地球之外同样产生影响。诗篇24:1宣告：“地和其中所充满的，世界和住在其间的，都属雅伟。”这一原则呼吁我们对所有受造物，无论远近，都负起负责任的管家职分。我们探索新领域的雄心，应与保护其原始面貌的承诺相平衡，以反映其神圣所有者的关怀。

verse.textEn: The earth is Yahweh's, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it.
verse.textZh: 地和其中所充满的，世界和住在其间的，都属雅伟。

title.en: Democracy is at stake when foolish humans bet on machines being intelligent | Rafael Behr
title.zh: 当愚蠢的人类押注机器智能时，民主就岌岌可危 | 拉斐尔·贝尔

summary.en: The article argues that democracy is jeopardized when human leaders unwisely place their trust in artificial intelligence. It highlights the critical need for enlightened leadership, particularly from the US president, to advocate for global AI regulation, contrasting this need with current political realities.
summary.zh: 文章指出，当人类领导者不明智地将信任寄托于人工智能时，民主就会受到威胁。它强调了开明领导人（特别是美国总统）推动全球人工智能监管的迫切需求，并将其与当前的政治现实进行了对比。

body.en: We need an enlightened US president to make the case for global AI regulation. Donald Trump is the exact opposite of what is needed When I am woken by the sound of my dog whining, I understand that she is hungry and wants me to get up. When my alarm clock goes off, I don’t consider its needs. It is following an instruction to rouse me at a certain time but it doesn’t care if I stay in bed. It doesn’t try to get me up by other means. The dog, on the other hand, will go to plan B. She barks. This capacity for autonomous action was once a difference between animals and machines. AI has blurred the line . Advanced models devise their own strategies to reach a goal. The task might be defined by a human master, but the machine weighs its options for delivery. It can make its own choices. Given rules, it can break them. Continue reading...
body.zh: 我们需要一位开明的美国总统来为全球人工智能监管提供理由。唐纳德·特朗普与我们所需要的恰恰相反。当我被狗的哀鸣声吵醒时，我知道她饿了，想让我起床。当我的闹钟响起时，我不会考虑它的需求。它会按照指令在特定时间叫醒我，但它并不关心我是否留在床上。它不会试图通过其他方式让我起床。另一方面，狗会执行 B 计划。她会吠叫。这种自主行动的能力曾经是动物和机器之间的区别。人工智能已经模糊了界限。先进的模型会制定自己的策略来实现目标。该任务可能由人类主人定义，但机器会权衡其交付选项。它可以做出自己的选择。既定规则，它可能会打破它们。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence challenges us to consider the limits of human understanding and the wisdom needed to govern powerful new technologies. As we navigate this complex future, Yahweh's word reminds us not to lean solely on our own intellect or creations, but to seek a deeper, divine wisdom. True discernment comes from trusting in...
reflection.zh: 人工智能的迅速发展促使我们思考人类理解的局限性，以及管理强大新兴科技所需的智慧。当我们驾驭这个复杂的未来时，雅伟的话语提醒我们不要单单依靠自己的智力或创造物，而要寻求更深层的、来自雅伟的智慧。真正的洞察力来自于全心信靠雅伟，尤其是在面对影响社会根基的决策时。

verse.textEn: Trust in Yahweh with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding.
verse.textZh: 你要专心仰赖雅伟，不可倚靠自己的聪明。

title.en: A moment that changed me: I found a forbidden novel – it led to a dangerous, lasting love
title.zh: 一个改变我的时刻：我发现了一本禁书——它带来了一段危险而持久的爱

summary.en: A Uyghur woman recounts how finding a forbidden novel in Xinjiang led her to embrace her culture and a lasting love, despite societal disapproval.
summary.zh: 一位维吾尔族女性讲述了她在新疆发现一本禁书后，如何因此拥抱自己的文化并找到一份持久的爱，尽管这在社会上受到非议。

body.en: Growing up in the Chinese region of Xinjiang, romance was frowned upon – as was much of my Uyghur culture. But one day, exploring a strange house, I found a gateway to both worlds Many people have a book that changes their life. For me and my wife, one book in particular changed our destinies for ever. We have been in love since we were teenagers, and today we are happily married – all because I accidentally discovered a forbidden novel in someone else’s house. It was a hot summer’s evening in 2009, in Kumul, Xinjiang. I was 16 and my father insisted I accompany him to visit a distant relative, where they would spend hours chatting about the old days and feasting as if they hadn’t eaten in years. As the well-behaved teenager I tried to be, I sat politely, nodding at their stories and pretending to absorb their “life lessons”, attempting to hide my boredom. The living room, with its small windows and bright lighting, was unbearable. Continue reading...
body.zh: 我在中国新疆地区长大，浪漫是不受欢迎的——就像我的维吾尔文化一样。但有一天，在探索一栋陌生的房子时，我发现了通往两个世界的大门许多人都有一本改变他们生活的书。对于我和我的妻子来说，有一本书永远改变了我们的命运。我们从少年时就相爱，到今天幸福地结婚了——这一切都是因为我无意中在别人家里发现了一本禁书。 2009年，新疆哈密尔一个炎热的夏夜。我当时 16 岁，父亲坚持让我陪他去拜访一位远房亲戚，他们会花上几个小时谈论过去的时光，然后大吃大喝，就好像他们已经很多年没有吃饭一样了。作为一个我努力成为的乖孩子，我礼貌地坐着，对他们的故事点头，假装吸收他们的“人生教训”，试图隐藏我的无聊。客厅的窗户很小，灯光明亮，令人难以忍受。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story highlights the courage to follow one's heart and embrace one's identity, even when cultural norms or authorities forbid it. It reminds us that there are times when our deepest convictions, aligned with Yahweh's truth, call us to a path different from what human systems dictate.
reflection.zh: 这个故事彰显了追随内心、拥抱自我身份的勇气，即便文化规范或权威禁止。它提醒我们，有时我们最深刻的信念，与雅伟的真理相符，会召唤我们走一条不同于人类体系所规定的道路。

verse.textEn: We must obey God rather than human beings!
verse.textZh: 顺从神，不顺从人，是应当的。

Four people familiar with the matter told Reuters that the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), which oversees the US ⁠telecommunications industry, is developing a measure to bar imports of new ​Chinese optical transceivers, which allow data to travel over fiber-optic cables at the speed of light within datacenters. Officials hope to publish the measure this year, according to Reuters. Continue reading...

reflection.en: In a world of complex technological dependencies and geopolitical tensions, nations often seek to anticipate and mitigate potential risks. Proverbs 27:12 reminds us of the wisdom in foreseeing danger and taking prudent steps to protect what is valuable. Such foresight, applied with integrity, can guide leaders in navigating intricate global challenges.
reflection.zh: 在一个技术相互依赖和地缘政治紧张复杂的世界中，各国常常寻求预见并减轻潜在风险。箴言27:12提醒我们，预见危险并采取审慎措施保护宝贵之物是智慧之举。这种以正直为基础的远见，能够指引领导者应对错综复杂的全球挑战。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: Stock market turmoil sheds stark light on the opaque AI economy
title.zh: 股市动荡揭示不透明的人工智能经济

In moments when investors scramble to make sense of unpredictable developments, Proverbs 3:5 reminds us to lean not on our own understanding, but to trust in Yahweh with all our heart. This...

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

title.en: This tiny NSW town is set to become a $560m US defence 'cornerstone'
title.zh: 这个新南威尔士州小镇将成为耗资 5.6 亿美元的美国国防“基石”

summary.en: Fifield will host the world's first primary scandium mine after a Pentagon deal aimed at countering China.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A remote Australian town is set to become a "cornerstone" of the Western supply of scandium, a rare earth mineral needed for defence, planes, and data centres after local mining company Sunrise Energy Metals secured a US$400 million ($566m) pledge.

The Pentagon revealed the details of the conditional loan commitment to Sunrise to build the world's first primary mine for scandium, of which China dominates supply and processing, at a meeting between US President Donald Trump and mining executives in Washington.

Scandium is usually sourced as a byproduct of other mining and is found throughout the Earth's crust in low concentrations.

"We aim to establish Syerston as a cornerstone of Western scandium supply," Sunrise chairman Robert Friedland said in a statement, referring to the proposed mine in Fifield, New South Wales.

Fifield is a remote town in the centre of the state, roughly 450 kilometres west of Sydney. 2016 census data shows just 129 people live in the town that boasts a single pub.

NSW has some of the highest concentrations of scandium globally, Resources Minister Madeline King said.

"The Sunrise scandium project hosts the world's largest and highest-grade known scandium resource, which has a range of vital aerospace, defence and clean energy applications," she said.

"No one country alone can create secure, end-to-end supply chains in critical minerals and rare earths.

"In working together, Australian mining companies can create more jobs and investment opportunities here at home, and more jobs and investment in the United States."

King described the announcement as a "significant vote of confidence" in Australia's capacity to supply the US and its allies with the minerals they need.

China restricted exports of scandium for defence products last year, triggering the US search for new suppliers.

The Pentagon statement said the scandium project will "ensure Western alignment from mine to finished product".

"Secretary Hegseth and Deputy Secretary Feinberg are mobilizing the Department of War's resources to secure our critical mineral supply chain," said Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering.

Trump and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese signed a critical minerals agreement aimed at countering China in October, pledging that each would invest $1 billion in projects.

On Saturday, Trump announced that the US was reclaiming its place as the "minerals superpower of the world."

title.en: Wildlife under threat as bird flu spreads among natives in a second state
title.zh: 禽流感在第二个州的当地人中传播，野生动物受到威胁

summary.en: There have now been 215 confirmed or presumed positive detections of the deadly virus in Australia.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及受造之物关怀与环保责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The deadly bird flu virus has spread to native birds in another state, as the national tally continues its steep rise across the country.

Two greater crested terns returned positive for the H5 flu strain in NSW, with one found near Narooma on the state's south coast and the other near Wentworth close to Mildura, officials confirmed on Saturday.

There have now been 215 confirmed or presumed positive detections, although the poultry industry remains clear of the virus so far.

It's the first time that avian influenza has been detected in an Australian native bird in NSW, with the state now recording four cases.

"These positive cases are not unexpected. We have been preparing for a situation like this, and we remain well equipped to respond to manage further impacts," Environment Minister Penny Sharpe said.

Surveillance in the impacted areas is continuing to ensure early detection of any further cases, the government added.

Testing at CSIRO's Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness confirmed on Saturday a further 10 detections of bird flu, all from greater crested terns in Victoria's southwest and Melbourne.

There were 28 positive detections in South Australia among wild seabirds, mostly among greater crested terns, with 15 of those on the state's Limestone Coast and 11 on Kangaroo Island, Australia's Chief Veterinary Officer Beth Cookson said.

SA chief vet Skye Fruean said there was no particular reason why the state had so far encountered most of Australia's confirmed cases.

"Unfortunately, we were just unlucky to be the first place where this did spread into our resident birds," she told ABC.

"I expect there will be other spread in other states and territories with time but ... I don't know how quickly that will happen."

Meanwhile in Victoria's southwest, avid birdwatcher Tracey Gray has been preparing alongside dedicated locals for the arrival of H5, abiding by the key advice: avoid, record, report.

Concerns grew this week when two sick birds were discovered on Port Fairy's Griffiths Island, a sanctuary for plants, birds and animals which also has a large breeding colony of short-tailed shearwaters.

While the birds, which included a crested tern and a suspected albatross, are yet to be confirmed to have the virus, the discovery is concerning.

"The (terns) are a local species that move up and down our coast from Portland, Yambuk to Port Fairy. They move, separate and nest together," Ms Gray told the Australian Associated Press news agency.

"We are concerned about them because that local transmission is potentially the largest issue here.

title.en: Kmart's Smart Glasses have sold out. Their popularity pushed a national privacy probe
title.zh: 凯马特的智能眼镜已售罄，其受欢迎程度引发了全国性的隐私调查

summary.en: Kmart's "Smart Glasses," which are surveillance wearables, have quickly sold out, leading to a national privacy investigation in Australia.
summary.zh: 凯马特（Kmart）的“智能眼镜”作为监控可穿戴设备已售罄，引发了澳大利亚全国性的隐私调查。

body.en:
The $89 Kmart alternative to Meta's artificial intelligence glasses has sold out. Its popularity has contributed to a government push to investigate privacy protections.

Released on 28 July, Anko's Smart Glasses were cleared from shelves across the country in under a week.

The product offered discreet surveillance technology to the mass market, selling for at least $200 less than premium Meta versions, which have been available for years.

The black-rimmed, clear-lens glasses can record high-definition video and snap photographs, which are then quickly transfered to smartphones.

Using HeyCyan software, users can also answer calls, listen to music and use an AI assistant.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Kmart is among many retailers, including Amazon, Temu and AliExpress, that are selling cheaper alternatives.

On Friday, the Attorney-General, Michelle Rowland, appealed to Australia's Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC) to investigate the potential privacy implications of smart glasses.

Rowland requested that the independent statutory agency give the issue priority consideration, citing serious safety concerns for women and children.

"Privacy is an essential part of all our lives; it allows us to be who we are with dignity and without fear," Rowland said.

"Unlike other forms of technology, smart glasses may be used more discreetly, making it harder to know when you are being recorded.

"The OAIC regularly monitors the effects of new technologies on privacy — and the government has every faith that they will identify any new privacy risks and mitigation measures."

Rowland said the government will also continue to contribute to work to ensure "privacy laws are fit for purpose in the digital age".

According to Privacy Commissioner Carly Kind, 85 per cent of Australians have become increasingly concerned about their personal privacy since 2021.

She said that protections under the Privacy Act don't extend to those filmed by smart glasses and that new laws must be considered.

"Australia’s Privacy Act only applies to businesses and government agencies, not to individuals, and it only applies when those entities collect personal information," Kind wrote in a post to the OAIC webpage.

“In circumstances where a tech company is receiving and storing personal information collected by surveillance wearables, they’ll have to make sure they’re complying with privacy law."

However, she questioned the company's capacity to notify individuals that they are being recorded.

title.en: House prices are falling, but first home buyers like Grace say corrections haven't helped
title.zh: 房价下跌，但像格蕾丝这样的首次购房者表示调整无济于事

summary.en: Despite an expected historical low in house prices this year, many first-home buyers in Australia, like Grace, find that homeownership remains unattainable.

body.en:
House prices are falling. But for Grace, buying her first home still comes with compromise.

The 29-year-old Wollongong resident and her partner began searching for their home earlier this year, conveniently as the market began trending down.

"It just happened to happen when I was ready to start looking," the 29-year-old told SBS News.

"We went into it pretty open-minded as we didn't know what we'd be able to afford, but heard prices may be dropping with the tax changes."

The pair had hoped to buy in the city where they live on NSW's south coast — but it's beyond their budget.

While the slump has made the market more attractive, Grace said there are still major issues.

"While the first home buyer scheme makes it more accessible to purchase a home, massive mortgage repayments are still a huge barrier, so I'll only buy somewhere where I can put down at least a 10 per cent deposit," she said.

"Another barrier is definitely bidding against those with clearly more money than you from the bank of mum and dad".

Money may be on the mind of many potential buyers, with new data reporting a significant drop in borrowing power since the start of 2026, thanks to the three consecutive Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) interest rate hikes seen so far this year.

New data from Canstar reveals that an average income earner's maximum borrowing capacity had fallen by an estimated $35,400 since January, while couples seeking to buy a property had theirs slashed by $70,700.

The February RBA interest rate hike dropped borrowing capacity by $12,200 for individuals and $24,400 for couples.

The March hike saw a drop of $11,800 and $23,600, and May's $11,400 and $22,700.

The RBA is expected to hold the cash rate at its next meeting on Tuesday. However, if Australians are subject to another rate hike, borrowing power would drop to $46,300 per person and $92,500 per couple.

Canstar's data insights director, Sally Tindall, said it's a "classic case of one step forward and one step back" for prospective buyers.

"While falling property prices may look like a win for people trying to get into the market, higher interest rates are keeping borrowing budgets in a bind," she said.

“The challenge for buyers is that a cheaper price tag doesn’t necessarily mean a more affordable home if your borrowing capacity has been cut at the same time."

“Headline inflation might have made a somewhat unexpected drop in June, but core inflation is still sticky," she said.

"The RBA might not hike on Tuesday, but it's difficult to see it ruling out further hikes altogether.

title.en: US-styled large trucks linked to a higher risk of pedestrian deaths, Australian study finds
title.zh: 澳大利亚研究发现，美式大型卡车与行人死亡风险增加有关

summary.en: A new Australian study has identified a link between US-styled large trucks and a higher risk of pedestrian fatalities, contributing to the rising rates of pedestrian deaths on Australian roads.
summary.zh: 一项新的澳大利亚研究发现，美式大型卡车与行人死亡风险增加有关，这导致澳大利亚道路上的行人死亡率不断上升。

body.en:
This trend is moving Australia further away from its Vision Zero ambition — a national commitment to eliminate all road deaths and serious injuries by 2050.

But what is driving the increase? And is the trend evenly distributed across different road users?

The answer to the first question is complex. The short answer to the second is no.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Historical data show that for much of the past two decades, population-adjusted fatality rates for pedestrians and car occupants (drivers and passengers) broadly followed the same downward trajectory.

But since 2021, the two trends have started to noticeably diverge. Pedestrian fatality rates have been rising, while those for drivers and passengers have remained relatively stable.

Does this indicate some systemic change in our road system? We know vehicles on Australian roads are getting progressively bigger: more protective of their own occupants, but potentially more dangerous to those outside them.

To find out, we conducted the first Australian study to investigate this question using detailed pedestrian crash data.

We linked each crash to the size and weight of the vehicle involved and developed statistical models to isolate the contribution of vehicle size while accounting for other important factors.

Data show the average footprint (the ground area covered by the car) of light vehicles in Australia has increased by around 7% since 2005.

For utes and US-style trucks, the increase has been even greater, approaching 18%.

This means the gap between conventional passenger cars and utes/US-style pick-up trucks continues to widen.

There are also more bigger cars on our roads. In 2012, of all new vehicles sold in Australia, only about one quarter were SUVs. By 2023, they accounted for 57%.

This transformation is reflected in the crash data too. Between 2012 and 2024, the average weight of passenger vehicles involved in pedestrian crashes in Victoria rose from about 1,440 kilograms to 1,570 kg – an increase of around 130 kg (9%).

For years, evidence that larger passenger vehicles are more dangerous to pedestrians has come almost entirely from the United States.

To answer that question, we analysed 10,376 pedestrian crashes involving passenger vehicles in Victoria between 2012 and mid-2025. Heavy vehicles such as trucks and buses were excluded.

The crash records contained detailed information on the circumstances of every collision, including the road environment, speed limit, driver and pedestrian characteristics, time of day and other factors.

body.zh: 腐败监管机构正在调查有关天主教保守派自由党的指控，但其他人也被卷入听证会“我认为他们在捕鲸。我们只是还不知道他们会击中哪头鲸，”一位自由党内部人士在新南威尔士州反腐败独立委员会第二周听证会结束后表示。腐败监管机构正在调查一群被称为改革者的年轻自由党人士接受非法捐款的指控，这些捐款包括来自新南威尔士州天主教学校、一家酒店经营者和一名逃亡房地产开发商让·纳西夫（Jean Nassif）的捐款，以资助分支机构的堆积。改革者意图获得自由党的控制权，并最终在堕胎、安乐死、婚姻平等和气候变化方面推行更加保守的政策。继续阅读...

reflection.en: When those in positions of influence are found to be acting without integrity, it erodes public trust and can lead to widespread disillusionment. This investigation reminds us that Yahweh's word highlights the profound impact leaders have on society, where righteous governance brings joy and wicked rule brings distress. Ultimately, true authority is...
reflection.zh: 当身居要职者被发现缺乏诚信时，会侵蚀公众信任并可能导致普遍的幻灭。这项调查提醒我们，雅伟的话语强调了领袖对社会的深远影响，正直的治理带来喜乐，而邪恶的统治则带来痛苦。最终，真正的权威并非通过权势或地位建立，而是通过坚守公义和道德行为。

verse.textEn: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan.
verse.textZh: 义人增多，民就喜乐；恶人掌权，民就叹息。

title.en: Senior managers at St Basil’s aged care, where 50 died from Covid, can’t remember it all. Grieving loved ones can’t forget
title.zh: 圣巴西尔养老院50人死于新冠，高级经理称不记得所有细节，悲痛的亲人无法忘怀

summary.en: Senior managers from St Basil’s aged care facility testified at a coronial inquest into the deaths of 50 residents from Covid-19. The inquest resumed on the sixth anniversary of the tragedy, with grieving families present in court.
summary.zh: 圣巴西尔养老院的高级经理们在一次死因调查中作证，该调查旨在查明50名住户死于新冠肺炎的原因。此次调查在悲剧发生六周年之际恢复，悲痛的家属们出席了法庭。

body.en: Konstantin Kontis and Vicky Kos were compelled to testify at a coronial inquest resuming on the sixth anniversary of the tragedy Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Quiet sobs could be heard in Melbourne’s coroner’s court, as several families attended to finally hear from the pair who were the most senior managers when, throughout July and August 2020, almost a quarter of the 188 residents at St Basil’s aged care home died from Covid-19 or neglect . Following multiple failed legal bids to avoid giving evidence after 50 residents died in the Victorian aged care home they managed, Konstantin Kontis and Vicky Kos were compelled to testify at a coronial inquest resuming on the sixth anniversary of the tragedy. Continue reading...
body.zh: 康斯坦丁·康蒂斯 (Konstantin Kontis) 和维基·科斯 (Vicky Kos) 被迫在悲剧六周年纪念日恢复的验尸调查中作证 获取我们的突发新闻电子邮件、免费应用程序或每日新闻播客 2020 年 7 月和 8 月期间，St Basil 养老院 188 名居民中有近四分之一死亡，墨尔本验尸官法庭上可以听到安静的抽泣声，几个家庭最终听到了这对最高级管理人员的声音。来自 Covid-19 或疏忽。在他们管理的维多利亚式老年护理院有 50 名居民死亡后，康斯坦丁·康蒂斯 (Konstantin Kontis) 和维基·科斯 (Vicky Kos) 多次通过法律途径避免提供证据，但均以失败告终，他们被迫在悲剧六周年纪念日恢复的验尸调查中作证。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The painful contrast between managers who claim memory loss and families who cannot forget highlights the deep anguish when the elderly are forsaken in their vulnerability. Yahweh's word reminds us of the profound responsibility to care for those whose strength is spent, ensuring they are never cast off or forgotten.
reflection.zh: 经理们声称记忆模糊，而家属们却无法忘记，这种痛苦的对比凸显了老年人在脆弱时被遗弃的深切悲痛。雅伟的话语提醒我们，对那些年迈体衰者负有深重责任，要确保他们永不被抛弃或遗忘。

verse.textEn: Do not cast me away when I am old; do not forsake me when my strength is gone.
verse.textZh: 我年老的时候，求你不要丢弃我；我力气衰弱的时候，求你不要离弃我。

title.en: David Brat bound for Australia as diplomat confirmed as next US ambassador
title.zh: 大卫·布拉特被确认为下一任美国驻澳大利亚大使

summary.en: Former Republican state congressman David Brat has been confirmed by the US Senate as the next ambassador to Australia. Brat previously advocated for a merger of Christianity and capitalism.
summary.zh: 前共和党州议员大卫·布拉特已被美国参议院确认为下一任驻澳大利亚大使。布拉特曾主张将基督教与资本主义融合。

body.en: Former Republican state congressman, who once argued Christianity and capitalism should merge, confirmed by US Senate to fill long-vacant role Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Former Virginia congressman David Brat has been confirmed by the US Senate to be the next US ambassador to Australia, after the role had been left vacant for 18 months. Brat’s confirmation was among more than 70 votes pushed through the Senate by Republicans on Friday, Washington time, before the summer recess. Continue reading...
body.zh: 曾主张基督教和资本主义应该融合的前共和党州议员，被美国参议院确认填补长期空缺的职位 获取我们的突发新闻电子邮件、免费应用程序或每日新闻播客 弗吉尼亚州前国会议员戴维·布拉特 (David Brat) 已被美国参议院确认为下一任美国驻澳大利亚大使，此前该职位已空缺 18 个月。华盛顿时间周五夏季休会前，共和党人在参议院通过了 70 多票投票，布拉特的确认是其中之一。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The appointment of a diplomat who once advocated for merging Christianity and capitalism invites reflection on where our ultimate allegiance lies. Yahweh's teaching reminds us that we cannot serve two masters, urging us to consider the distinct demands of faith and worldly systems. This calls believers to discern carefully how their faith informs their...
reflection.zh: 一位曾主张将基督教与资本主义融合的外交官获得任命，这促使我们反思我们最终的忠诚归于何处。雅伟的教导提醒我们，人不能事奉两个主，敦促我们思考信仰与世俗体系之间不同的要求。这呼吁信徒们仔细辨别他们的信仰如何影响他们参与经济和政治生活，而不是将两者混为一谈。

verse.textEn: No one can serve two masters... You cannot serve both God and Mammon.
verse.textZh: 一个人不能事奉两个主……你们不能又事奉神，又事奉玛门。
